status: Verified public interaction and progression hotfix. Full public VR and AR grip journeys both complete the Causeway and enter the Archive. Physical-device and human-experience approval remain open.

publicAcceptance.sourceAndPostJourneyGates: All 102 files matched the same final manifest before public play and after each suite.
publicAcceptance.errors: VR, AR and Goldwind captured no JavaScript or console/shader errors. Homepage and production board recorded empty JavaScript error arrays; those reports do not collect a separate console-error array.

additionalPublicPreservation.scope: Both audited reports use the real public origin, have empty JavaScript/console-error arrays and match all 102 production files. Do not add these counts to a claim of physical-device certification.

nativeEvidence.additionalModelSample: 24 generated chapter routes used real model movement and checked 144 winch, relay and latch targets at both hand offsets. This is a finite model sample, not a rendered or hardware study.

diagnosis: The owner could fight and collect supplies but could not discover environmental actions or level completion. Pilgrimage wrote its action/objective text into an XR HUD suppressed by the default palm display. The existing palm panel showed combat status rather than mission requirements. Earlier campaign tests used other input paths and did not establish that Goldwind grip progression was discoverable in headset play.
implemented: A nearby world-space prompt identifies the actual available winch, relay, latch or exit and its configured control. The default left-bow Goldwind binding remains left grip. The free hand can point or reach toward the same nearby control and squeeze grip, subject to hand range and line of sight. This invokes the existing game interaction rather than assigning mechanism or objective state. A consumed grip remains consumed until release so it cannot repeatedly toggle or turn into a disk throw. Pickup, bow draw, quiver and disk ownership retain priority. Actual action feedback distinguishes blocked actions. The on-demand palm objective card shows required signals, progress and direction/distance to the next signal or ready exit; the reward screen names the next chapter.
completionContract: In the Causeway, restore both relay lanterns by a valid shot or nearby interaction, then use the far exit beacon and choose a blessing to enter the Ashen Archive. The Archive similarly requires its lenses before its exit. Killing every enemy is not required for these chapters. The older Endless exit retains its own warden requirement. Locked exits explain their real conditions; they are not bypassed by the new grip action.
revealingReview: The first complete native VR/AR journeys passed their functional checks, but screenshot inspection showed the added objective card clipping at the default hand pose. The card was moved above and beyond the palm while remaining hand-anchored. Final native view review and both complete public journeys project all four corners into both eyes and preserve the actual objective/exit textures. Initial clipped screenshots remain in the evidence bundle; the initial functional passes are not treated as visual approval. Low-resolution software-rendered stereo screenshots and crisp canvas textures do not establish physical-headset readability.
independentAudit: Recomputed 11 retained ZIP hashes against their GitHub artifact digests. All final public source archives match the same 102-file manifest, have the expected source revision and an empty uncommitted diff. Public reports, screenshots, routes, projection bounds and per-archive audits are retained. GitHub artifacts have finite retention; the final receipt is persistent repository evidence.
preserved: No saved layout identity, chapter dimensions, collision, enemy logic, objective requirements, rewards, save schema, profile/envelope key, canonical task ID or workbook byte changes. All five prior generators remain. Goldwind is still default; A/B golden arrows, trigger damage arrows, thrown disk, reach quiver, handedness, shield/interaction remap, classic crossbow, Xbox down-Blink/left-damage shortcuts, grip supplies and hand-pinch menus are preserved. AR expedition, Sanctuary and Architect's Table retain their distinct contracts. Current Prism and all sibling-game work were preserved; no temporary source-writing workflow entered master.
testingBoundary: Production WebGL and existing simulation were exercised using generated device buttons, sticks and poses. Title/pause/session setup used normal DOM and keyboard UI; once in XR, the full chapter used controller stick movement and grips, then a headset blessing choice. Tests do not assign player coordinates, health, resources, enemies or objectives. Local loopback browser access was blocked by administrator policy and was not bypassed or counted as a pass. Native/public browser evidence comes from the identified Actions runs.
remainingWork: Larger and longer chapters are not implemented by this hotfix. They are recorded as the next content priority, with purposeful route choices, pacing and recovery rather than simply stretched travel. Physical Quest 3/Xbox testing, varied seated/standing reach and readability, tracking/compositor behavior, comfort, sustained performance, unfamiliar/repeat-player comprehension and measured chapter duration remain open.
closureScope: This commit adds only a nested publication receipt. The already deployed and independently verified runtime, assets, defaults, saved worlds and planning workbook do not change.
